patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v3] mm: bypass swap readahead for zswap

version_history.subject: [PATCH v3] mm: bypass swap readahead for zswap

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch bypasses swap readahead for zswap, an in-memory synchronous backend similar to zram. The current implementation of swap readahead can lead to pointless prefetching of pages, causing increased anon residency and page cache thrashing. By bypassing readahead for zswap, the patch aims to reduce this overhead and improve performance. Measurements show significant gains in build time, zswap-in/out rates, and reduced swap readahead hits. The patch reuses existing code and adds a new helper function to check if a swap entry is synchronous.

review_comments.author: Barry Song
review_comments.summary:
Reviewer Barry Song questioned whether the performance gain from bypassing swap readahead for zswap is dependent on the page-cluster setting, suggesting testing with values 0 and 1 to confirm

Reviewer Barry Song expressed interest in knowing if similar performance gains would be observed when using specific configurations, and suggested adding a mention of the 'page-cluster' configuration to the changelog.

Gave Reviewed-by
review_comments.raw_body:
Hi Alexandre,

I assume your configuration is as below?

/ # cat /proc/sys/vm/page-cluster
3
/ # cat /sys/kernel/mm/swap/vma_ra_enabled
true

I am curious whether setting `/proc/sys/vm/page-cluster` to either 0
or 1 would result in the same performance gain on a zswap-enabled
system?

---

The change makes sense to me. I am just curious whether setting those
configurations would result in the same performance gain.

Maybe you can mention the `page-cluster` configuration in the changelog
as well.

review_comments.author: Yosry Ahmed
review_comments.summary: The reviewer notes a potential benefit of readahead for compressed swap, citing Kairui's LPC presentation, but acknowledges that this is not currently the case and assumes any future improvements would also apply to zswap.
review_comments.raw_body:
No objection here, I am just thinking about Kairui's LPC presentation
about how compressed swap can (in theory at least) still benefit from
readahead: https://lpc.events/event/20/contributions/2421/attachments/2116/4689/Better%20Anon%20(Swap)%20Readahead%20(2).pdf.

Seems like a big portion of the fault cost is still outside of
decompression and can benefit from readahead, but that isn't the case
today. I assume any future improvements to readahead and re-enabling
for zram would also cover zswap?

review_comments.author: Alexandre Ghiti
review_comments.summary:
Reviewer noted that the patch does not handle the case where zswap is disabled, and requested a check to be added to ensure that swap readahead is bypassed only when zswap is enabled.

Reviewer Alexandre Ghiti agreed to align zswap with zram, following Kairui's work, but no specific technical issue or suggestion was made.
sentiment_signals: patch needs additional handling for zswap disabled
review_comments.raw_body:

---

Thanks,

Alex

review_comments.author: Alexandre Ghiti
review_comments.summary:
Reviewer noted that the patch does not handle the case where zswap is enabled but the tree is empty, which can lead to a static branch in disk-only systems.

Reviewer noted that the patch description's performance metrics are not sufficient to justify bypassing swap readahead for zswap, and requested more detailed analysis.
review_comments.raw_body:

review_comments.author: Alexandre Ghiti
review_comments.summary:
Reviewer noted that the patch bypasses swap readahead for zswap, but questioned whether it's necessary to do so in all cases, as some systems may not have zswap enabled or may be disk-only.

The reviewer ran additional tests with a workload of kbuild -j16 in a 768M memcg, zswap only, and observed consistent performance gains from bypassing swap readahead for zswap, including reduced build time, zswap-in and zswap-out, and swap readahead pages. The reviewer also confirmed that the results were the same with page-cluster set to 0.
review_comments.raw_body:
Hi Barry,

On Fri, Oct 9, 2026 at 8:22 AM Alexandre Ghiti <alexghiti@meta.com> wrote:

---

So I ran the same workload (kbuild -j16, 768M memcg, zswap only, n=3 per arm):

    768M memcg (sustained swap thrash):
      metric                                        mm-new
page-cluster=1    page-cluster=0    + bypass
      build time (s)                               530.0      462.0
-12.8%      452.3  -14.7%    452.7  -14.6%
      zswap-in (GB)                               95.7        66.7
-30%         64.2    -33%     64.4    -33%
      zswap-out (GB)                           169.3      138.3
-18%       135.2    -20%    135.6    -20%
      swap readahead (pages)            8.37M     1.93M    -77%
  0      -100%    0.53M    -94%
      swap_ra hit (%)                            73.6        86.5
+13pp          -          -          90.7   +17pp

Exact same results with page-cluster to 0, so I'll add that to the
changelog as you suggested.

Thanks again for the review,

Alex

review_comments.author: Barry Song
review_comments.summary: Reviewer Barry Song noted that if a high-hit-rate readahead algorithm is developed, it may be necessary to map all readahead folios at the same time in do_swap_page() to avoid increasing total work for synchronous I/O.
review_comments.raw_body:
In that case, if we can develop an accurate readahead algorithm with a
high hit rate for readahead folios, we will probably also need to map
them at the same time, as proposed in [1]. For example, if we readahead
4 folios, we should map them all together in `do_swap_page()`.
Otherwise, the cost of future minor faults can still be comparable to
the decompression cost. Readahead alone would therefore increase the
total work, which can be quite significant for synchronous I/O.

[1] https://lore.kernel.org/linux-mm/CAGsJ_4xM=WnFO-OuwVude-DQ_UkaCi_zF_bXBP9Li5+ZPNy0VQ@mail.gmail.com/

Best Regards
Barry

review_comments.author: Barry Song
review_comments.summary: Reviewer Barry Song noted that setting page-cluster = 0 could resolve the issue without the patch, but is still pleased to see the auto-tuning patch.
review_comments.raw_body:
Thanks! This seems to be a strong indication that setting
`page-cluster = 0` can also resolve your problem, even without your
patch. :-)

But I'm still glad to see your auto-tuning patch!

Best Regards
Barry

review_comments.author: Nhat Pham
review_comments.summary:
Reviewer Nhat Pham noted that bypassing swap readahead for zswap may not be suitable when multiple tenants with different swap backends (compressed synchronous and async IO) coexist on the same host, potentially causing issues.

Reviewer Nhat Pham expressed concerns about doing synchronous readahead work in page fault, suggesting it feels wrong and may concentrate work of multiple pagefaults into a single pagefault. They proposed offloading readahead to an asynchronous worker as a potential solution.
review_comments.raw_body:
If every tenants use zswap, yes. But we have tenants with different
kinds of swap backend in the same host (some using compressed
synchronous swap backend, some async IO swap backend).

---

I think we need some smarter readahead work, for sure. I'm just not
quite sure what it'd look like in the end, though.

Doing synchronous readahead work in page fault feels wrong. I chatted
very briefly with Kairui about this. Kairui is trying to come up with
smarter readahead heuristics, but I don't know - even if it's 100%
hitrate, we're concentrating work of multiple pagefaults into a single
pagefault. That sounds off to me?

Crazy idea time - what if instead of skipping readahead for
zswap/zram, we offload it to asynchronous worker (only synchronously
loading the target page)? That'll cancel out the latency issue at
least...?

review_comments.author: Barry Song
review_comments.summary: Reviewer Barry Song noted that asynchronous wake-up latency is highly unpredictable and can be much longer than the time it takes to complete mapping and decompression work in do_swap_page(), which makes async zram readahead unreliable without hardware queues.
review_comments.raw_body:
I am quite sure I tried this 3 or 4 months ago, and the
performance was very poor. The problem is that async wake-up
latency is highly unpredictable. For example, do_swap_page()
can complete all the mapping and decompression work in less
than 10 us. However, if we queue the work to an async thread,
its wake-up latency alone could be much longer than 10 us.

Based on my results, async zram readahead only works if we have
hardware queues rather than relying on async threads.

Best Regards
Barry

review_comments.author: Barry Song
review_comments.summary: Reviewer Barry Song noted that the patch bypassing swap readahead for zswap might miss some folios in the readahead window that are actually in zswap, and vice versa, but suggested not handling this complexity at this point.
review_comments.raw_body:
Yep, I have no objection to this patch. As I replied to
Alexandre, I was just curious about what would happen if we
set `page-cluster` to 0.

I think Alexandre's autotuning patch looks good overall. We
just have a lot of corner cases to consider. For example, we
might miss zswap and trigger readahead, even though some
folios in the readahead window are actually in zswap. The
opposite could also happen.

However, I don't think we need to handle all this complexity
at this point.

Best Regards
Barry

review_comments.author: Kairui Song
review_comments.summary: Reviewer Kairui Song suggested bypassing swap readahead for zswap, but noted that a better readahead policy is needed to avoid increased unmapping costs. They proposed evaluating shadow as a stronger hint for readahead and implementing proactive aging or a similar approach.
review_comments.raw_body:
That's a really nice POC! We should do that IMO, maybe with better
support for (m)THP readahead too.

We first need a better readahead policy though, or else unmapping
these folios might cost even more.

For the readahead part I'm thinking about evaluating using shadow as a
stronger hint for readahead after MGLRU-FG which helps distribute the
folios based on frequencey more evenly among gens, also with a more
proactive aging (async aging, or maybe lru_gen_imbalanced as Barry
once suggested somewhere) so folios in the same gen with same freq
will be much more likely to be reused. Or something similiar to file
readahead's PG_readahead based readahead. Well more
experiments are needed first though.

review_comments.author: Nhat Pham
review_comments.summary: reviewer asked about potential regressions with the zswap shrinker enabled and both zswap and disk swap backends present
review_comments.raw_body:
Would there be regression with shrinker on, when we have mixed zswap
and disk swap backends?
